another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text: I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit! Let me start the eligibility assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Let me start by asking about the child you're claiming for:

**What is the age of the child you want to claim Child Benefit for?**

Please choose one of these age categories:
- **Under 16** - Children aged 15 or younger
- **16 to 19** - Teenagers aged 16, 17, 18, or 19 (may need to be in education/training)
- **20 or over** - Adults aged 20 and above

Which category applies to your child?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text:
Hello! I'm interested in claiming Child Benefit and would like to know if I'm eligible.

My child is 18 years old, so that would be in the 16 to 19 category.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for that information! So you have an 18-year-old child. Let me navigate to the next step of the assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Now I need to check your 18-year-old's current situation:

**Is your child currently in education or training, or have they recently left education?**

Please select one of these options:
- **Currently in education or training** - They're studying full-time at school, college, university, or in an approved training programme
- **Recently left education** - They finished education within the last 20 weeks
- **Neither** - They're not in education/training and didn't leave recently

Which applies to your child?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Neither - they're not in education or training, and they didn't leave recently either.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for clarifying that. Let me navigate to the outcome based on this information.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'm sorry to inform you that based on the information provided, you would **not be eligible for Child Benefit** for your 18-year-old child.

**Here's why:**

For an 18-year-old to qualify for Child Benefit, they must be:
- In approved full-time education (such as school, college, or university), OR
- In an approved training programme

Since your child is no longer in education or training and didn't leave education recently (within the last 20 weeks), they don't meet the eligibility criteria.

**Important to know:**
- Child Benefit can continue for young people aged 16-19 if they're in approved education or training
- If a 16-17 year old leaves education, benefit can sometimes continue for up to 20 weeks if they register with the careers service or armed services
- Once a child reaches 20, they automatically stop being a qualifying child for Child Benefit

**What you can do:**
If you believe your child might return to education or training, you could potentially make a claim at that point. Otherwise, if you have other children under 16 (or aged 16-19 in education), you may be able to claim for them instead.

Is there anything else I can help you with, or do you have other children you'd like me to check eligibility for?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text:
I understand. Thank you for explaining that to me. No, Alex is my only child, so it sounds like I'm not eligible. I appreciate your help in clarifying this.
